mainTopic: When a baby, including a slave born to a שפחה, is circumcised on the eighth day versus right away, and when a newborn is no longer considered a possible נפל.
overview: This amud opens at the end of an answer: proofs from before מתן תורה do not count, because the הלכה was renewed at סיני. רב אסי had taught that a baby whose birth does not make his mother טמאה לידה, such as a יוצא דופן, is not circumcised on the eighth day. The גמרא challenges him from a מחלוקת between רב הונא and רב חייא בר רב about breaking שבת for a יוצא דופן. It answers that the שבת question and the eighth-day question depend on each other. Next the גמרא shows that רב אסי's idea is a מחלוקת תנאים, quoting a ברייתא about slaves circumcised at one day or at eight days. רב חמא makes it depend on whether the mother's טבילה came before the birth, while the תנא קמא requires eight days anyway. רבא shows that רבי חמא can explain all four cases and asks how the תנא קמא can have a home-born slave circumcised at one day. רבי ירמיה and רב משרשיא each supply such a case. Finally, a ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that a baby who lives 30 days, or an animal that lives 8 days, is not a נפל. The גמרא begins to ask whether a baby under 30 days is a ספק, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The הלכה was renewed at סיני
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the previous answer: proofs from before מתן תורה do not count, because the הלכה was renewed at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of an answer that started on the previous section. The גמרא is finishing its point that we cannot learn today's הלכה from what was done before the תורה was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof had been brought from the time of אברהם אבינו against רב אסי. The answer is that once the תורה was given at סיני, the laws were given fresh. So practices from before סיני cannot disprove רב אסי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: was renewed, given anew
the law as it applies in practice

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The full answer is 'נתנה תורה בסיני ונתחדשה הלכה', which means 'the תורה was given at סיני and the הלכה was renewed.' Only the last part appears here.

phrases.english: and the halacha was renewed.
phrases.notes: The end of the previous answer, which rejects a proof from before סיני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer earlier that defended רב אסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical distinction: laws from before Sinai are not binding precedent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Practices from before מתן תורה cannot disprove רב אסי.

steps.title: Challenge from the dispute about a C-section baby
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חייא בר רב argue only about whether we break שבת for a יוצא דופן. That implies both agree he is circumcised at eight days, which goes against רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But it was taught: about a baby born by C-section and one who has two foreskins, רב הונא and רב חייא בר רב argued. One said we break שבת for his מילה, and one said we do not. They only argue about breaking שבת. But at eight days we certainly circumcise him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי's rule. It quotes an argument about a C-section baby in which both sides seem to agree that he gets מילה on the eighth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יוצא דופן does not make his mother טמאה לידה. So by רב אסי's rule he should not have מילה on the eighth day at all. The argument between the אמוראים is only about שבת, which suggests that eighth-day מילה is agreed upon. That contradicts רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)
a baby born through the side, by C-section
two foreskins
we break שבת for him, meaning his מילה overrides שבת
we certainly circumcise him

phrases.english: Is that so? But wasn't it stated:
a child born by caesarean section
and one who has two foreskins,

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chiyya bar Rav disagreed:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: מְחַלְּלִין עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was turned away, the גמרא brings a new challenge from an אמורא-level מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that a baby whose mother is not טמאה לידה is not circumcised on the eighth day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sides limit their argument to שבת. That implies both agree a יוצא דופן is circumcised on the eighth day, which contradicts רב אסי.

steps.title: The two questions depend on each other
steps.stepSummary: The eighth-day question and the שבת question are linked, so the one who does not break שבת also holds there is no eighth-day obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument about שבת is really also an argument about the eighth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one who says we break שבת holds that a יוצא דופן must be circumcised on the eighth day. The one who says we do not break שבת holds that there is no eighth-day obligation at all, just like רב אסי. So רב אסי has a supporter, and the implied agreement falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: this depends on that; the two issues are linked

phrases.english: This depends on that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rejecting the assumption that the eighth-day question was agreed upon.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the inference by linking the two questions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was only about שבת, with the eighth day agreed upon.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whoever does not break שבת also holds there is no eighth-day obligation, which matches רב אסי.
steps.whatToRemember: For a יוצא דופן, the questions of 'eighth day' and 'breaking שבת' go together. Only an eighth-day מילה overrides שבת.

steps.title: A parallel tannaitic teaching about slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב אסי's idea matches a מחלוקת תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא: some slaves are circumcised at one day and some at eight days.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a dispute of תנאים: There is a home-born slave who is circumcised at one day, and there is a home-born slave who is circumcised at eight days. There is a slave bought with money who is circumcised at one day, and there is a slave bought with money who is circumcised at eight days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows that רב אסי's question was already debated by תנאים. This step sets up a ברייתא that will be explained in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that a slave's מילה is not always on the eighth day. Sometimes it is done right away, at one day. The details of each case will show when the eighth-day rule applies and when it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: like a dispute of תנאים
a slave born in the owner's home
a slave bought with money
circumcised at one day, meaning right away

phrases.english: It is like a tannaitic dispute:
there is a home-born slave who is circumcised at one day
and there is a home-born slave circumcised at eight days;
there is a slave bought with money who is circumcised at one day
and there is a slave bought with money circumcised at eight days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב אסי, the גמרא links his view to an earlier מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both home-born slaves and bought slaves can sometimes be circumcised at one day and sometimes at eight days.

steps.title: Explaining the bought slave cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains: a slave born after his pregnant mother was bought is circumcised at eight days. A slave bought together with his mother after birth is circumcised at one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a bought slave circumcised at one day and a bought slave circumcised at eight days. How so? If he bought a pregnant maidservant and afterward she gave birth, that is a bought slave circumcised at eight days. If he bought a maidservant together with her child, that is a bought slave circumcised at one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא defines its cases. It explains when a slave bought with money gets מילה at eight days and when he gets it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby is born while the mother already belongs to the Jewish owner, the normal eighth-day rule applies. If a baby who was already born is bought along with his mother, there is no eighth-day count in the owner's home, so the owner circumcises him as soon as he acquires him. The גמרא will soon show how these cases connect to רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (the ברייתא asks this to explain its own cases)
a pregnant maidservant
and her child with her

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that both cases here are מקנת כסף, slaves bought with money. Even the baby born after the purchase counts as 'bought,' because he was bought inside his mother. The יליד בית cases are not explained here.

phrases.english: There is a slave bought with money who is circumcised at one day

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ מִקְנַת כֶּסֶף שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה, כֵּיצַד?
phrases.english: and there is a slave bought with money circumcised at eight days. How so?
If he bought a pregnant maidservant

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא מִקְנַת כֶּסֶף שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: this is a bought slave who is circumcised at one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ מִקְנַת כֶּסֶף שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לְאֶחָד וְיֵשׁ מִקְנַת כֶּסֶף שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה, כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא goes back and explains the cases it listed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave born after his pregnant mother was bought is circumcised at eight days. A slave bought together with his mother after birth is circumcised right away.

steps.title: The ברייתא's case of a home-born slave circumcised at eight days
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא explains how a יליד בית can be circumcised at eight days. The master bought a שפחה, she became pregnant while in his house, and she gave birth there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is a home-born slave who is circumcised at eight days. How so? A man bought a maidservant, she became pregnant while with him, and she gave birth. That is the home-born slave who is circumcised at eight days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of slave cases. It now explains when a slave born in the master's house waits until the eighth day for ברית מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the pregnancy itself started after the master owned the mother. The תנא קמא does not mention her טבילה at all. He seems to make the eight-day rule depend only on the baby being conceived and born in the Jewish household.

keyTerms.meaning: A home-born slave, born in the master's household
A non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew
She became pregnant while in his possession
How so? (introduces an explanation of a case)

phrases.english: And there is a home-born slave who is circumcised at eight days,
how so?
He bought a maidservant, she became pregnant while with him, and she gave birth
this is the home-born slave who is circumcised at eight days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ יְלִיד בַּיִת שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמֹנָה, כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 5 by giving the home-born, eight-day case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave conceived and born in the master's household is circumcised at eight days.

steps.title: רב חמא: it depends on whether the טבילה came before the birth
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא says the timing of the mother's טבילה decides the case. If the birth came before the טבילה, the baby is circumcised at one day. If the טבילה came first, the baby is circumcised at eight days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא says: If she gave birth and afterward he immersed her, that is a home-born slave circumcised at one day. If he immersed her and afterward she gave birth, that is a home-born slave circumcised at eight days.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא, רב חמא, makes a distinction. For him, what matters is whether the mother had already gone to the מקוה as a שפחה when she gave birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טבילה gives the שפחה her status, with some מצוות. Only after it can she become טמאה לידה. So for רב חמא, the eight-day rule depends on whether the birth made the mother טמאה לידה. If it did not, the baby is circumcised right away.

keyTerms.meaning: He had her immerse in a מקוה, which gives her the status of a שפחה
At one day, meaning right away, on the day of birth

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'one day' does not mean the baby is a day old. It means the baby is circumcised right away, on the day of birth, with no eight-day wait.

phrases.english: Rav Chama says:
If she gave birth and afterward he immersed her
that is a home-born slave circumcised at one day.
If he immersed her and afterward she gave birth
that is a home-born slave circumcised at eight days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view to the תנא קמא's case in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a home-born slave, the order of birth and טבילה decides the day of מילה. Birth before טבילה means one day. טבילה before birth means eight days.

steps.title: The תנא קמא makes no distinction, even without טומאת לידה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא does not care about the order of טבילה and birth. Even when the mother is not טמאה לידה, the baby is circumcised at eight days. So the מחלוקת matches the question of רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא does not distinguish between a case where he immersed her and then she gave birth, and a case where she gave birth and then he immersed her. Even though the mother is not טמאה לידה, the baby is circumcised at eight days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now speaks in its own voice to explain the תנא קמא. It shows that the two תנאים really disagree about רב אסי's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי linked the eight-day rule to the mother being טמאה לידה. רב חמא agrees with him: no טומאת לידה means no eight-day wait. The תנא קמא requires eight days even without טומאת לידה, so he disagrees with רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
It makes no difference to him; he does not distinguish
Ritually impure because of childbirth
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: רב חמא matches רב אסי: the eight-day wait depends on the mother being טמאה לידה. The תנא קמא disagrees and requires eight days for any יליד בית born in the house.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the job announced in step 4. It shows that רב אסי's idea is really a מחלוקת תנאים, so רב אסי has a תנא who backs him.

phrases.english: And the first Tanna does not distinguish
between a case where he immersed her and then she gave birth
and a case where she gave birth and then he immersed her,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין אִמּוֹ טְמֵאָה לֵידָה,
phrases.english: for even though his mother is not impure from childbirth,
he is circumcised at eight days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the תנא קמא's view against רב חמא's distinction in step 7, and ties the מחלוקת back to רב אסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a יליד בית is circumcised at eight days even if his mother was not טמאה לידה.

steps.title: רבא: under רבי חמא all four cases work, starting with the home-born ones
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a challenge with בשלמא. The ברייתא implies four types: home-born at one day, home-born at eight days, bought-with-money at one day, and bought-with-money at eight days. רבא shows how רבי חמא's view explains the two home-born cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It works well according to רבי חמא. You can find a home-born slave circumcised at one day, a home-born slave circumcised at eight days, a slave bought with money circumcised at one day, and a slave bought with money circumcised at eight days. If she gave birth and afterward he immersed her, that is a home-born slave circumcised at one day. If he immersed her and afterward she gave birth, that is a home-born slave circumcised at eight days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up a challenge against the תנא קמא. First he shows that רבי חמא's view easily explains all four cases. The 'but according to the תנא קמא' half comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means 'this view works fine.' It hints that the other view will have trouble. For רבי חמא, the order of טבילה and birth naturally produces both home-born cases. For the תנא קמא, a home-born slave at one day seems impossible, since a slave born in the house waits eight days even before his mother's טבילה. Steps 12 and 14 answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (sets up a contrast with a view that has trouble)
You can find it; such a case exists
A slave acquired by a money purchase

phrases.english: Rava said:
It works well according to Rabbi Chama,
you can find
a home-born slave circumcised at one day,
a home-born slave circumcised at eight days,
a slave bought with money circumcised at one day,
and a slave bought with money circumcised at eight days:

that is a home-born slave circumcised at one day.
If he immersed her and afterward she gave birth
that is a home-born slave circumcised at eight days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מחלוקת is mapped in step 8, רבא tests which view fits all the categories the ברייתא implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's view, that every home-born slave is circumcised at eight days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies four categories. רבי חמא can explain all of them. The תנא קמא seems unable to produce a home-born slave circumcised at one day. That point is spelled out in step 11.

steps.title: רבא continues: the two purchased-slave cases under רבי חמא
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes showing how רבי חמא explains the purchased slaves. Buying a pregnant שפחה, then having her immerse before the birth, gives a purchased slave circumcised at eight days. If one person bought the mother and another person bought her fetus, the fetus is circumcised at one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave bought with money is circumcised at eight days when the master bought a pregnant maidservant, immersed her, and afterward she gave birth. A slave bought with money is circumcised at one day when one person bought the maidservant and another person bought her fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes the 'works well' half of his challenge. He shows that under רבי חמא, both purchased-slave cases can also be found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the eight-day case, the baby was bought along with his pregnant mother. She then had her טבילה before giving birth, so she became טמאה לידה. In the one-day case, the baby's owner has no share in the mother. So her status does not link to the baby, and he is circumcised right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Pregnant
Her fetus
For example, such as (introduces a sample case)
This one... and that one (two different people)

steps.whyThisMatters: Now רבי חמא has explained all four categories. This sets up the coming question of how the תנא קמא can produce the same four cases.

phrases.english: A slave bought with money circumcised at eight days
is for example where he bought a pregnant maidservant
and immersed her, and afterward she gave birth.
A slave bought with money circumcised at one day

phrases.aramaic: — כְּגוֹן שֶׁלָּקַח זֶה שִׁפְחָה, וְזֶה עוּבָּרָהּ.
phrases.english: is for example where this person bought a maidservant, and that person bought her fetus.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְנַת כֶּסֶף נִימּוֹל לִשְׁמֹנָה כְּגוֹן שֶׁלָּקַח שִׁפְחָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's בשלמא from step 9, moving from the home-born cases to the purchased cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By showing that רבי חמא explains all four cases cleanly, רבא prepares to argue that the תנא קמא cannot do the same.

steps.title: How Can the תנא קמא Have a Home-Born Baby Circumcised at One Day?
steps.stepSummary: רבא completes his challenge to the תנא קמא: the other cases work for him, but the case of a יליד בית circumcised at one day seems impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the תנא קמא: granted, you can find all the other cases. But a home-born child circumcised at one day, how can you find that case?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now finishes the challenge he opened with בשלמא in step 9. After showing that רב חמא's view explains all four cases, he asks how the תנא קמא can explain a home-born baby who is circumcised at one day. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, a baby born in the master's house is circumcised at eight days, even if the mother had not yet immersed. That makes a 'home-born at one day' case look impossible. Yet the ברייתא implies that such a case exists.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא
A slave born in the master's house
Circumcised on day one, right away
How can you find such a case?

steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the תנא קמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every birth in the master's house gives eight days, the ברייתא's implied category 'home-born at one day' cannot exist.

steps.title: Buying a Maidservant Only for Her Fetus
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the case is where the master bought only the fetus, not the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is the case of one who buys a שפחה for her fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question. The master bought only the unborn baby, while the mother stays with her original owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby is born already owned by this master, so he is a יליד בית. But the mother is not this master's שפחה, so the eight-day rule does not apply, and the baby is circumcised at one day.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buys a maidservant
For her fetus only

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
In the case of one who buys a maidservant for her fetus.
phrases.notes: He owns the fetus but not the mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: בְּלוֹקֵחַ שִׁפְחָה לְעוּבָּרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by finding a case that fits.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every home-born baby must be circumcised at eight days according to the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: When only the fetus was bought, the baby is home-born but circumcised at one day, because the mother is not his.

steps.title: Does Buying the Fetus Count as Buying the Mother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי ירמיה's answer works only for the view that owning the 'fruits' is not owning the body. For the opposite view, it fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says that owning the produce is not like owning the body itself. But for the one who says that owning the produce is like owning the body itself, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי ירמיה. His answer depends on a known מחלוקת about whether owning the produce counts as owning the item itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that owning the produce of something counts as owning the thing itself (קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי). On that view, owning the fetus means you own the mother too. Then the mother is the master's שפחה, and we are back to eight days.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one opinion)
Owning the produce or benefit of something
Owning the item itself
What can be said? (there is a problem)

phrases.notes: Here the fetus is the 'produce' and the mother is the 'body'.

owning the produce is like owning the body itself,
what can be said?

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'פירות' does not mean fruit from a tree. In this case it refers to the fetus, the 'product' of the שפחה.
steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's answer from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's case of buying only the fetus
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If owning the fetus counts as owning the mother, the mother is the master's שפחה, so the baby should be circumcised at eight days.

steps.title: Buying a Maidservant on Condition Not to Immerse Her
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא gives a case that works for every view: the master bought the שפחה on condition that he will not immerse her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: It is the case of one who buys a שפחה on condition that he will not immerse her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא answers the challenge with a new case. The master owns the mother but agrees never to immerse her as a שפחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without that טבילה, the mother stays a non-Jew and never enters the status of a Jewish שפחה. Her baby is born in the Jew's house, so he is a יליד בית, but he is circumcised at one day. This answer does not depend on the קנין פירות question at all.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that
To immerse her (making her a שפחה with Jewish obligations)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא קמא, a home-born baby is circumcised at one day only when the mother is not the master's own שפחה. רבי ירמיה's example is buying only her fetus, so the mother is not his. רב משרשיא's example is buying her on condition not to immerse her, so she never becomes a שפחה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the eight-day rule for a slave depends on the mother being a proper שפחה, not just on the baby being born in the house.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
In the case of one who buys a maidservant
on condition that he will not immerse her.
phrases.notes: She remains a non-Jew, so her baby is circumcised at one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: בְּלוֹקֵחַ שִׁפְחָה עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא לְהַטְבִּילָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 13 challenge with a case that works even if קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without רבי ירמיה's fetus case, the תנא קמא has no home-born one-day baby.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שפחה bought on condition not to be immersed gives a home-born baby circumcised at one day, according to every view.

steps.title: Thirty days for a person, eight days for an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that a person who lives 30 days and an animal that lives 8 days are not considered a נפל. He proves each from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, any human baby that has lived thirty days is not a נפל, as it says: 'And their redemption, from a month old you shall redeem.' An animal that has lived eight days is not a נפל, as it says: 'And from the eighth day and on it will be accepted as an offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sets a time limit. After that point a newborn is treated as a normal, viable life and not as a נפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a person, the proof is פדיון הבכור, which only starts 'from a month old'. That shows that before 30 days the תורה does not yet treat the baby as a settled life. For an animal, the proof is that it can only be brought as a קרבן from the eighth day. That shows 8 days is the point where an animal is fully established as viable.

keyTerms.meaning: Remained or lasted, meaning stayed alive
A non-viable newborn that is not expected to live
'And their redemption, from a month old you shall redeem', the פסוק about פדיון הבכור
It will be accepted as an offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This 30-day line affects many הלכות about newborns, such as mourning, inheritance, and יבום. The גמרא will build on it right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the slave-circumcision cases to a related ברייתא about when a newborn is established as viable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who has lived 30 days, or an animal that has lived 8 days, is not a נפל.

steps.title: Before thirty days, is the baby a doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that a baby who has not yet lived 30 days has a doubtful status.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if the baby did not last thirty days, it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the flip side of the ברייתא: a baby who has not reached 30 days is a ספק נפל. This is a setup line, preparing the next question about what that doubt means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said what happens after 30 days. The גמרא now spells out the hidden other half: before 30 days we are unsure whether the baby is viable. This raises the next question: in which practical cases do we treat this baby as a ספק?

keyTerms.meaning: But if it did not last (an inference from what the source left unsaid)
It is a doubt

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying every baby under 30 days is surely a נפל. It is only saying the baby's status is uncertain until 30 days pass.

phrases.english: This implies: if it did not last (thirty days), it is a doubt?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading this out of the ברייתא's wording, and it sets up the next part of the discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the opposite inference from the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ברייתא mean that before 30 days the baby's viability is in doubt, and what follows from that?
